Sleep apnoea is when breathing stops and starts during sleep.
The NHS lists the main signs as pauses in breathing while asleep, gasping, snorting or choking noises, waking often and loud snoring.
Asthma + Lung UK gives doctors a simple prompt known as the Triple S: snoring, stopping breathing and excessive sleepiness.

sentence: The effects carry into the day.

In obstructive sleep apnoea the muscles of the upper airway relax during sleep, so the throat narrows or closes.
Breathing then stops and restarts.

Asthma + Lung UK says the risk is higher in people with asthma, especially if they are overweight, have gastro-oesophageal reflux disease or have asthma that is difficult to control.
